March 19, 2024

A powerful tool at every stage of product development, prototyping can take many different forms. These resources will help you level up your process, whether you’re new to prototyping or ready to dive deeper.

1.  [Cover the basics](https://www.figma.com/blog/23-prototyping-resources-to-bookmark-right-now/#cover-the-basics)
2.  [Level up your presentations](https://www.figma.com/blog/23-prototyping-resources-to-bookmark-right-now/#level-up-your-presentations)
3.  [Learn about video, motion, and flow](https://www.figma.com/blog/23-prototyping-resources-to-bookmark-right-now/#learn-about-video-motion-and-flow)
4.  [Go deeper with variables](https://www.figma.com/blog/23-prototyping-resources-to-bookmark-right-now/#go-deeper-with-variables)
5.  [Catch up on office hours](https://www.figma.com/blog/23-prototyping-resources-to-bookmark-right-now/#catch-up-on-office-hours)

From pumping up a presentation, to conducting user research, to facilitating feedback from stakeholders, [prototyping is instrumental in helping your team align](https://www.figma.com/blog/why-cultivating-a-prototyping-culture-will-help-you-build-better-products/?fuid=1237464931354017914)

on a shared vision. What you learn through prototyping helps you iterate and, ultimately, ship a better product.

On the heels of a suite of [prototyping enhancements](https://www.figma.com/blog/behind-the-feature-the-multiple-lives-of-multi-edit/?fuid=1237464931354017914)

, we’ve curated a comprehensive list of resources to get you going on your Figma prototyping journey, from informative livestreams and hands-on community files, to quick videos and social posts. Whatever your learning style, you’ll find plenty to take your skills up a notch.

## [Cover the basics](#cover-the-basics)

Start with these primers to get a sense of how to use prototyping to calibrate and accelerate the product development process.

[**Video: Build prototypes (8 minutes)**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lTIeZ2ahEkQ)

Get an overview of building an interactive prototype, including animation and incorporating feedback from your testers.

[**Video: Prototyping playlist (50 minutes)**](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLXDU_eVOJTx7aqRW3Skp1aRT9ktC3ctqA)

Dive into a snackable YouTube playlist that covers easing curves, transitions, smart animate, scrolling and device frames, and more.

[**Video: Prototyping 101 (63 minutes)**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UUsysuFmVrA)

Learn about basic frame-to-frame navigation in prototypes as well as more advanced capabilities you can unlock with features like interactive components.

[**Video: Learning Figma as a product person (Part 1) (7 minutes)**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ypLVdu-srt4)

See how to create a lightweight prototype as a non-designer working on the product side, and follow along in the community file below.

[**Video: Learning Figma as a product person (Part 2) (17 minutes)**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=81mwcN9g1nc)

In part two of the series, learn how to use transitions, smart animate, scroll behaviors, and other tips to help bring your prototypes to life.

[**Community file: Accessible prototypes in Figma**](https://www.figma.com/community/file/1167124335986833540)

Discover Figma’s accessibility mode for prototypes, which means screen readers like VoiceOver (Mac) and JAWS (Windows) can read information about designs when you’re presenting them in prototyping mode.

Ana Boyer is a designer advocate at Figma, where she is building community and empowering design teams across industries. She believes in collaboration and iteration and is always looking to build systems and establish processes where there is ambiguity.
